questions.stem_markdown: A cyclist is travelling along a straight horizontal road at a speed of 4 m s⁻¹ when she passes a point O. She accelerates at a constant rate for a distance of 42 m, reaching a speed of V m s⁻¹. She maintains the speed of V m s⁻¹ for 50 m and then decelerates at 2 m s⁻² before coming to rest. The distance travelled while decelerating is 16 m.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For use of constant acceleration to get a correct equation in $$V$$ only.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Acceleration section : $$42 = \frac{(4 + (theirV))}{2} t \quad [t = 7]$$ Deceleration section: $$0 = (theirV) - 2t$$ or $$16 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2t^2$$ or $$16 = (theirV)t - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2t^2 \quad [t = 4]$$ For constant speed section $$t = \frac{50}{theirV} \quad [t = 6.25]$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For attempt to find an equation in $$t$$ during acceleration or deceleration or constant speed. Using their $$V$$, $$s = 16$$, $$a = -2$$, $$u = 4$$. Must lead to a positive $$t$$.
For attempt to find an equation in $$t$$ for the other 2 sections. Using their $$V$$, $$s = 16$$, $$a = -2$$, $$u = 4$$. Must lead to a positive $$t$$.
AWRT 17.3 from correct work

parts.prompt_markdown:
The aeroplane is flying horizontally. The aeroplane’s engines are producing a constant power of 5500 kW, and the aeroplane experiences a constant horizontal resistance force of 25 kN.

Find the speed of the aeroplane.

The aeroplane then ascends 300 m in 50 s, while maintaining the same speed. The resistance force is no longer constant, and the work done against the resistance force in ascending the 300 m is 270 000 kJ. The mass of the aeroplane is 60 000 kg.

Find the average power of the aeroplane’s engines.

skills: Relate power to force and speed
Use work-energy relation for work against resistance
Calculate speed from power/force balance
Use average power = total work / time
methods: Work done = force × distance (or via work-energy)
subtopics: Power with constant force and speed

questions.stem_markdown: Three particles P, Q and R, of masses 0.6 kg, 0.4 kg and 0.8 kg respectively, are at rest in a straight line on a smooth horizontal plane. The distance from P to Q is 3 m, and the distance from Q to R is also 3 m (see diagram). P is projected directly towards Q with speed 3 m s⁻¹. After P and Q collide, P continues to move in the same direction with speed 1.5 m s⁻¹.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Attempt at conservation of momentum. 3 non-zero terms. Allow sign errors.
OE must be positive. Allow max **M1A0** if $g$ included with the masses.
OE condone including $g$ if already penalised in (a). FT their 2.25. speed = $\frac{\text{their } 2.25}{3}$

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: $Q \text{ takes } \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \left[ = \frac{4}{3} \right] \text{ s to reach the point at which } R \text{ was initially.$

Difference in speeds of $P$ and $QR = 1.5 - \text{their } 0.75 [= 0.75] \text{ m s}^{-1}$ so time = $$\pm \left[ \frac{3 - \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \times 1.5}{1.5 - \text{their } 0.75} \right]$$ OR $$(\text{their } 0.75) t \pm \left( 3 - \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \times 1.5 \right) = 1.5t \left[ \rightarrow t = \frac{4}{3} \right]$$ OR $$(\text{their } 0.75) \left( T \mp \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \right) \pm 3 = 1.5T \left[ \rightarrow T = \frac{8}{3} \right]$$ OR $$(\text{their } 0.75) \left( T' \mp \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \mp \frac{3}{3} \right) \pm 3 = 1.5 \left( T' \mp \frac{3}{3} \right) \left[ \rightarrow T' = \frac{11}{3} \right]$$ OR $$(\text{their } 0.75) \left( T' \mp \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \mp \frac{3}{3} \right) = 1.5 \left( T' \mp \frac{3}{3} \mp \frac{3}{1.5} \right) \left[ \rightarrow T' = \frac{11}{3} \right]$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Dependent on both previous **B** marks. For attempt to find time.
Allow 3.67 s.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: $Q \text{ takes } \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \left[ = \frac{4}{3} \right] \text{ s to reach the point at which } R \text{ was initially.}$

$P \text{ takes } \frac{3}{1.5} [= 2] \text{ s to reach the point at which } R \text{ was initially, so combined particle has travelled for } \frac{3}{1.5} - \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \left[ = \frac{2}{3} \right] \text{ s beyond where } R \text{ was initially.}$ So combined particle is $\left( \frac{3}{1.5} - \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \right) \times (\text{their } 0.75) [= 0.5] \text{ m beyond where } R \text{ was initially.$

Difference in speeds of $P$ and $QR = 1.5 - \text{their } 0.75 [= 0.75] \text{ ms}^{-1}$ so time $$= \pm \left[ \frac{\left( \frac{3}{1.5} - \frac{3}{\text{their } 2.25} \right) \times (\text{their } 0.75)}{1.5 - \text{their } 0.75} \right] \left[ = \frac{2}{3} \right]$$
